text.tspan: Give every member a shared tag, switch on it, and TypeScript knows exactly which shape you are holding.
kind is the DISCRIMINANT: a literal type unique to each member.
s is narrowed to the circle member.
s.radius is available; s.side is an error.
s.side is available, and nothing else.
All three handled, so s is never here; it compiles.
Add a fourth member and THIS LINE fails to compile,
which is how you are told to update the switch.
Why a tag beats a guess
Without a discriminant you end up probing
for properties ('radius' in s), which breaks
the moment two members share a field.
A literal tag is unambiguous, cheap at run
time, and survives JSON, so the same union
works for data off the network.
